subject: Runbook handoff + module catalog sync for Zephyr private stack
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Tan <paul.tan@zephyrfin.com>
Cc: Akiko Sato <akiko@zephyrfin.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Runbook handoff + module catalog sync for Zephyr private stack

Paul / Akiko —

Following up from last week's kick-off, attaching the first-pass runbook and a compact module matrix that maps Terraform/Helm/Ansible pieces to the private VPC topology you shared. Key points in this handoff: 

- Runbook v1 contains environment bootstrap, artifact verification (GPG + SHA256), and rollback playbooks for the most common failure modes.
- Module matrix describes ownership, required inputs, outputs, and gating tests that must pass in GitLab CI before a promotion.
- We recommend enabling the "artifact-signature-check" job in the pipeline for air-gapped installs; it is currently optional but listed in the checklist.

Ask: can your infra team confirm the NAT/proxy IP ranges in the attached spreadsheet (column D) so we can pin egress rules in the Terraform modules? If you can reply with a short confirmation or a corrected CSV by EOD tomorrow, we can queue the MR that wires these values into the tfvars and the Helm value-overrides.

Next steps we plan on our side: Marissa will open a merge request that adds the module catalog to your infra repo and Karthik will add a CI job that fails the merge if signatures are missing. 

Attachments: privstack-runbook-v1.pdf, terraform-module-matrix.csv, gitlab-ci-pipeline-checklist.md

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Paul Tan <paul.tan@zephyrfin.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Akiko Sato <akiko@zephyrfin.com>, Zephyr Legal <legal@zephyrfin.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 11:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Runbook handoff + module catalog sync for Zephyr private stack

Ava —

Thanks for the docs and the clear checklist. A couple of quick clarifications from our side before we sign off on the TF vars: 

1) NAT egress ranges: we will confirm but note that two of the ranges in the spreadsheet are managed by our network provider and may change during their maintenance window (Nov 18-19). If your Terraform expects fixed ranges for security groups, we need a short lived exception window or use a CIDR that covers both ranges.
2) Artifact verification: we prefer HSM-backed signing for the production install; is the repo workflow compatible with an HSM signing step (we use CloudHSM)?

Legal has asked for a short appendix describing access patterns for audit (who can trigger a manual rollback, read-only ACLs for SRE, duration of logs). Can you have that included in runbook v2?

Paul
Head of Infrastructure
Zephyr Financial
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Tan <paul.tan@zephyrfin.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 13:09:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Runbook handoff + module catalog sync for Zephyr private stack

Paul —

Couple of technical notes to address the questions: 

- NAT ranges: the Terraform modules accept either explicit cidr_list (recommended for static infra) or an external data source (we have a small module that pulls the ranges from a JSON endpoint and writes the tfvars during CI). If your provider rotates ranges, we can wire the data-source approach so deployments always use the active list.
- HSM signing: the pipeline has a pluggable signing step. We currently have examples for AWS KMS and an on-host GPG flow; integrating CloudHSM will need a short helper script that calls the HSM SDK to sign release artifacts. It is compatible — we'll produce a sample job in the MR.
- Access & audit appendix: we'll add an appendix to runbook v2 documenting the roles that can execute promote/rollback jobs, the GitLab audit events that must be retained, and recommended retention windows.

Action items I will take:
1) Draft the CloudHSM signing stub and push as a sibling MR.
2) Add the data-source pattern and test it in the staging pipeline (I will mark the job with an explicit gate so it doesn't auto-promote).

I will also call out where the Helm charts expect the proxy to exist (values.proxy.external) so you can validate ingress rules.

- Karthik
Staff Engineer, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Tan <paul.tan@zephyrfin.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 08:44:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Runbook handoff + module catalog sync for Zephyr private stack

Paul / team —

From a compliance standpoint, three minimal asks before we finalize runbook v2: 

1) Artifact provenance: we need signed SBOMs for each release artifact. Add a pipeline step that emits an SPDX JSON and attaches it to the artifact archive.
2) Audit retention: confirm 365-day retention for deploy/audit logs in the initial contract (we can shorten to 90 days for staging). Put this in the appendix for Legal.
3) Secrets handling: the Terraform modules must not render secrets into Helm values in plain text. Use a KMS-backed secret provider or templates that read from Vault at runtime; document the pattern in the runbook.

Irene
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

>

If your provider rotates ranges, we can wire the data-source approach so deployments always use the active list.

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Tan <paul.tan@zephyrfin.com>
Cc: Akiko Sato <akiko@zephyrfin.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 15:23:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Runbook handoff + module catalog sync for Zephyr private stack

Paul —

Thanks for the quick feedback. Agreed on all points. To summarize commitments and timeline: 

- We will produce runbook v2 by Mon 11/9 that includes the Legal appendix and the audit retention language (Irene will sign off on the wording).
- Karthik will open the CloudHSM signing MR and a small example job by Friday 11/6.
- Marissa will open the catalog MR and enable the artifact-signature-check pipeline gate for your repo; you can toggle the gate once you've validated the HSM job.
- Please confirm whether the provider-maintained NAT ranges should be covered by a CIDR umbrella or by a data-source pull. If we don't hear back by 11/6 we will default to the data-source approach.

I've attached the runbook and the CSV again for convenience. If Legal wants different phrasing in the appendix, loop them into the reply and we'll iterate.

Best,
Ava
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: privstack-runbook-v1.pdf, terraform-module-matrix.csv
